name: Dog Park at Gore Street Park
desc: Convert part of Gore Street Park (Gold Star Mother’s Park) into a dog park with clear signage, a clean area for dogs to run, benches, and water fountains for dogs and owners.

name: Amphitheater in Danehy Park
desc: Build an amphitheater in Danehy Park for outdoor performances, music, stories, and other cultural events that the whole community can enjoy.

name: Bus Shelter Monitors with Real Time Arrival
desc: Install 2 real time bus arrival monitors with digital displays at the bus shelters at Cambridge Street & Hampshire Street and Cambridge Street & Inman Street.

name: Little Free Libraries (Book Exchanges)
locationText: 13 locations - 1 in each neighborhood.  Focus on parks, community gardens, or dog parks.
desc: Informal Book Exchanges are already popular in Cambridge on streets and at the DPW yard. This project would install 13 Little Free Libraries (Book Exchanges) to support literacy, community engagement, and fun throughout the streets of our city.

name: Furniture for the O’Connell Library
desc: The furniture at the O’Connell library is quite worn down. This proposal would provide the library with new tables, chairs, computer workstations, and loveseats for parents and children to read together.

name: North Cambridge Community Garden
locationText: Russell Field where Harvey Street meets Alewife Linear Park.
desc: The new North Cambridge Community Garden in the northeast corner of Russell Field will build community, provide healthy food, and promote wellness and environmental awareness

name: Materials for Planting by Residents on Public Land
desc: Raised beds for food plants, placed at sites around town determined by city staff, consulting with residents. Plant materials, such as flower bulbs, for planting on other city land, distributed to residents in several locations.

name: Traffic Garden
locationText: Location to be determined through a community process.
desc: A Dutch Traffic Garden, called “Safety School” in the U.S., is a permanent park for children to learn transportation etiquette by role playing. Kids take turns biking, walking, and driving a miniature streetscape in a safe environment.

name: Outdoor Bodyweight Fitness Equipment in Danehy Park
desc: Install outdoor body-weight fitness equipment for stretching, strength building, and plyometric exercises at Danehy Park

name: Cambridge Garden of Peace
locationText: An area within Riverside Press Park at River Street & Memorial Drive.
desc: The Peace Garden memorial will include benches and stones or objects reflecting names of loved ones from Cambridge who lost their lives to violence.  An area of Riverside Press Park will be transformed into a place of tranquility and reflection.

name: Mural Project at Russell Field
desc: A middle-school student in North Cambridge proposed installing a mural in his neighborhood that “shows the community of Cambridge.” The mural will be installed on the Russell Field Fieldhouse.

name: Wayfinding Banners - Neighborhood & Commercial Identity
desc: Hang banners in 13 strategic high-traffic, high-density business and neighborhood areas to identify commercial and/or neighborhood-specific local areas in Cambridge.  This would support commerce, diversity, and neighborhood integrity.

name: Renovation of Bus Shelter at Comeau Field & Rindge Ave
locationText: Rindge Avenue at Comeau Field, North Cambridge.
desc: This project entails a major redesign and renovation, with community participation, of the 83 bus shelter. New features will include acrylic panels with cut-out figures and a roof element evocative of nearby recreation and natural habitat.

name: Raymond Park Community Garden Improvements
desc: Beautify the community garden at Raymond Park through the addition of fencing, a partial retaining wall, landscaping and plantings, and furnishings.

name: Healthy Trees for a Healthy Cambridge!
locationText: Sidewalks in East Cambridge, Wellington/Harrington, Area IV/Port, and Cambridgeport.
desc: Street trees cool the city, absorb pollution, and make our neighborhoods more livable! Vote to plant 100 new trees & build tree wells in the areas that need them most, along with educational signage so you can learn about your “green neighbors.”

name: Computers for the Community Learning Center
desc: At the Community Learning Center the students can improve their English or pursue a High School Equivalency Diploma. The CLC has 18 laptops and 12 ThinkPads for 630 adult learners. They want to get 20 additional laptops, keyboards, mice and storage cart for the students.

name: Bilingual Books for Children Learning English
desc: This project will fund the purchase of 300-350 bilingual books for Cambridge children in the Agenda for Children’s Literacy Initiative project

name: Central Square PublicToilet (Toilet for All)
desc: 24-hour access public toilet near Central Square, similar to the one currently underway in Harvard Square. The exact location will be determined through a public process.

name: Bike Repair Stations
desc: Install 8 bike repair stations with tools and bike pumps around the City for cyclists to quickly, easily, and freely fix routine bike problems.  Locations include 2 libraries, 2 T stops, 3 parks (includes Inman Sq), and Fresh Pond Parkway.

name: Free Wifi in 6 Outdoor Public Spaces
locationText: Public space outside 4 Youth Centers, the Golf Course, and Water Department.
desc: Install special outdoor wifi access points to offer free public wifi in the public space surrounding the Area IV, Frisoli, Gately, and Moore Youth Centers, as well as the Fresh Pond Golf Course and Cambridge Water Department.

name: Free Wifi and Soofa Benches in 3 Parks
locationText: Wifi and Soofa benches in Lopez, Raymond & Dana Parks; Soofa benches in Porter & Inman Squares and the Main Library.
desc: This project would install free public wifi in 3 Cambridge parks that are in areas with limited access to free wifi and 10 solar-powered benches that allow residents and visitors to charge their electronic devices for free in public areas.

name: Invention and Production of Music
desc: Install music studios and equipment at the Frisoli, Gately, and Russell Youth Centers to inspire creativity, enable pre-teens and teens to express their skills and passions, and provide youth with another recreational outlet.

name: Real-Time Bus Arrival Monitors in Harvard Square
desc: Real-time bus arrival monitors at 2 bus stops in Harvard Square will inform travelers when the next bus will arrive, so they can adjust their plans if needed.

name: Little Free Libraries (Book Exchanges)
desc: Informal Book Exchanges are already popular in Cambridge on streets and at the Public Works yard. This project would install 13 Little Free Libraries to support literacy, community engagement, and fun throughout the streets of our city.

name: Remodel the Kitchen at the Frisoli Youth Center
desc: The kitchen area in the Frisoli Youth Center is in dire need of renovating. Replace the stove, dishwasher, cabinets, and countertops in the Frisoli Youth Center kitchen. This project can serve many Cambridge youth!

name: Inclusive Playground for All Kids
locationText: Location to be determined through a community process.
desc: This Universal Design playground would include equipment that is designed to be usable by everyone without special adaptations or retrofitting. This is greatly needed to create inclusive physical environments in the community.

name: Outdoor Exercise Equipment
desc: Installing outdoor exercise equipment similar to the fitness stations along the Charles River in Boston at Danehy Park and three other Cambridge parks would provide a health benefit for the whole community.

name: Interactive Technology for the Main Library
desc: This project will fund an iPad lending kiosk and 16 iPads, as well as a permanent interactive screen in the Children’s Room of the Main Library.

name: The Sustainable Energy Pilot
locationText: War Memorial Recreation Center and 1 City parking lot.
desc: Picture a future where Cambridge residents are making sustainable energy choices. Let’s start now – install energy conversion devices on gym equipment and a rapid electric vehicle charging station.

name: Block Party Trailer with Party Equipment
desc: A vehicle or trailer, equipped with supplies needed for bringing neighbors together at outdoor block parties.

name: Wellington-Harrington Community Garden
locationText: Location to be determined through a community process.
desc: The Wellington-Harrington neighborhood is full of gardeners but has no community gardens. Let’s support our neighbors’ desire to bring a community garden to Wellington-Harrington. They’ve organized, we’ve listened - let’s make it happen!

name: Volleyball Court at Danehy Park
desc: Creating an outdoor volleyball court would be an exciting addition to the city, especially since there is not currently an outdoor court in all of Cambridge! The court would have sand and a sturdy net for three-season usage.

name: Cambridge Garden of Peace
locationText: Location to be determined through a community process.
desc: The Peace Garden will include a memorial for loved ones from Cambridge whose lives were taken due to violence. The Peace Garden will be a place of tranquility and reflection.

name: Veterans' Garden
locationText: Location to be determined through a community process.
desc: Veterans of war often return home with severe but unseen injuries. 8,000 veterans, each year, take their own lives. A garden design to heal the wounds of war for vets and their families is the purpose of this project. Help make it possible.

name: Nursing Pod for Mothers and Infants
desc: Provide an attractive private space where working mothers and community members can breastfeed or pump during the work day. Provision of break time and a private area for nursing or pumping is required by the Fair Labor Standards Act.

name: Digital Sign at City Hall in Multiple Languages
desc: Digital sign that will scroll announcements in multiple languages and welcome people to Cambridge. It will be easily seen when residents go by and will be a prototype that if successful can be replicated in other areas of the city.

name: Cambridge Prepared Food Rescue Freezer Van
desc: Let’s feed the hungry in our city. A freezer van is the vital piece of equipment that would allow Cambridge and its partners to potentially double prepared food rescue deliveries from roughly 3,500 healthy frozen meals to 7,000 each week.

name: New Chairs for Cambridge Public Schools!
desc: We need new chairs in CPS schools, specifically the Cambridge Rindge and Latin School (CRLS), Cambridge Street Upper School, Putnam Avenue Upper School, and Rindge Avenue Upper School.

name: Separate Bike Lanes from Traffic
desc: Improve safety for drivers and bikers by moving bike lanes to be between street parking spots and the sidewalk, reducing car-bike interactions and potential collisions.

name: 5 Water Bottle Refill Stations
desc: At a water bottle refill station you get a healthy drink for free! The Cambridge Public Health Department recommends drinking more water and less sugary drinks.

name: Make Massachusetts Avenue Safer for Bikers
desc: Improve safety on Massachusetts Avenue by adding shared lane markings for bicycles, along with signs saying “Bike Route,” “Bicycle May Use Full Lane,” and “Watch for Cyclists” where bike lanes are not already present.

name: Shape Up Our Squares!
desc: Paint green bike lanes through the intersections on Massachusetts Avenue in Central Square and Hampshire Street in Inman Square to improve safety for drivers, bikers, and pedestrians.

name: Faster, Better #1 Bus for Cambridge
desc: Increase on-time trips and reduce bus commuter transit times for the #1 Bus on Massachusetts Avenue by installing a Transit Signal Priority system at intersections allowing buses to extend green lights to get through traffic faster.

name: Safer Crosswalks For Busy Roads
desc: Install flashing light signs on six crosswalks that pedestrians can activate before crossing the street. These flashing signs make drivers more aware of crossing pedestrians to help prevent crashes, especially at night.

name: Solar-Powered Real-Time Bus Tracker Displays
desc: This project proposes installing 10 solar-powered bus tracking displays with real-time arrival information at high-use bus stops throughout the City of Cambridge.

name: Kinetic Energy Tiles
desc: Kinetic energy tiles are tiles that generate energy from your footsteps! We want to introduce these tiles into our city and get Cambridge residents involved with clean energy! These tiles can power streetlights, phones, or laptops.

name: Solar Power Shines!
desc: Let’s power the public library with clean, renewable energy!  Adding solar panels to our main library will help Cambridge meet our climate goals by reducing emissions, saving money over time, and serving as an example for patrons.

name: Hydration Stations In Four Locations
desc: Additional water fountains and bottle refill stations will help residents stay hydrated and reduce waste from plastic bottles! One of the new fountains will be designed to reflect Cambridge, like the artistic water fountain at Fresh Pond.

name: Upgrade The Moore Youth Center
desc: The Moore Youth Center is outdated compared to other youth centers. New furniture and equipment will help bring more youth to the center.

name: Cambridge Street Art Trail
desc: Commission local artists to create a series of murals and street art reflecting Cambridge's vibrancy and diversity. Increase space for publicly created street art (like that in "Graffiti Alley" in Central Square).

name: Danehy Park: Fitness, Signs, Dog Park Lights & Scoreboards
desc: This project will bring much-needed improvements to Danehy Park, with great positive impact for Cambridge residents. New fitness equipment, signs, dog park lights for evening use, and scoreboards will make Danehy Park better utilized.

name: Building A Strong And Safe Bike Community
locationText: Main Public Library and public schools.
desc: Cambridge has cyclists aged under 8 to over 80. To educate and protect bicyclists and bicycles, we propose offering free helmets with safety training for grade school students and installing an artistic bike shelter at the Main Library.

name: Universal Design: Playgrounds for Everyone!
locationText: 1-2 playgrounds to be determined by community process.
desc: Universal Design playground equipment is designed to be usable by everyone without special adaptations or retrofitting. Let’s go beyond legally required minimum accessibility standards to ensure our playgrounds truly welcome everyone!

name: (2-3) Level 2 Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
desc: Adding electric vehicle charging stations to crowded neighborhoods without garages will send a powerful message that now is the time we can all buy electric cars.  We will reduce pollution and support a transition to clean transportation.

name: Little Free Libraries For Children
desc: Little free libraries are beautiful, functional works of art that help build community. They develop literacy skills and encourage a love of reading by making it easy for families to exchange books in an informal, neighborhood setting.

name: Safe Naps For Cambridge Preschoolers!
locationText: King Open & Peabody Preschools, Baby U, Center for Families.
desc: New healthy PVC-free nap mats will help Cambridge preschoolers sleep safely! We will purchase 80 mats for programs still using old mats that are coated with PVC, a chemical associated with negative health effects. All kids in Cambridge preschools deserve a safe nap!

name: Bicycle Desks For Cambridge Students
locationText: CRLS and the four Upper Schools.
desc: Bicycle desks will help bring focus and exercise to Cambridge classrooms as well as improve the physical and mental health of students.

name: Shade and Wet Weather Canopies for Playgrounds
desc: Installing canopies over playgrounds that do not have protection from the elements will reduce weather-related safety concerns and increase playground availability and use.

name: Free Public Wi-Fi In Columbia Park
desc: Internet access is an essential right. Adding free Wi-Fi to Columbia Park (Clement G. Morgan Park) will enable people to access information for school and work.

name: All-In-One Mobile Performance Stage & Art Space
desc: Spread the love and joy of arts and music in the city of Cambridge! Residents can bring world-class arts and musical performance to any city street, any time, regardless of age, race, or background.

name: Wireless Speakers For Youth Centers
desc: Adding wireless surround sound speakers to the youth centers benefits young people doing homework, playing basketball, and other activities. Bringing music to the youth centers will bring more youth to these centers.

name: Lighting Landmarks: CHLS Gate & Sumner Statue
locationText: Broadway & Ellery Street, Harvard Square-MacArthur Park.
desc: Effective light design for Cambridge landmarks can make our city as livable at night as in the day. Well-designed lighting would enhance these landmarks and increase public safety.

name: Learn about Nature in the Port
desc: Artistic signs would educate children and adults about nature in the city. The signs would contain information about local wildlife and the ecosystems and would include a map of habitats around Cambridge.

name: Drive on Superpower: Electric Vehicle Charging
desc: Dreaming of a Tesla but don’t know where to charge it? Twelve fast-charging electric vehicle ports throughout the City’s municipal lots will encourage environmentally friendly driving habits!

name: 100 Trees for a Cleaner, Greener Cambridge
locationText: Barren sidewalks in East & North Cambridge.
desc: Let’s green our streets by planting 100 trees in neighborhoods lacking foliage! From cooling heat islands to cleaning our air, these trees will be a long-term investment in making our city a healthier, happier place.

name: Critical Resource Kits for the Homeless
desc: Deliver resource kits to homeless residents through established programs. These kits will provide supplies such as socks, feminine hygiene products, toiletries, first aid kits, and other items to Cambridge’s most vulnerable population

name: Flashing Crosswalks for Safer Streets
desc: This project would fund rapid flashing beacons at 10 high pedestrian risk crosswalks. These beacons increase the visibility of pedestrians, especially at night. They can alert drivers to crossing pedestrians, thereby preventing crashes.

name: Drinking Water Across More Parks
desc: Install new water fountain/bottle-fillers at up to 10 parks that lack drinking water fixtures. This will ensure that more residents can enjoy free, clean, drinking water at their local park, no matter which neighborhood they call home.

name: New Musical Instruments for CRLS
desc: New music instruments for CRLS would encourage and support arts education for Cambridge students. Newer equipment at the high school would not only benefit high school students but middle school students as well.

name: Jade Chain: Living Moss Walls to Combat Pollution
locationText: Porter, Inman & Harvard Squares, Binney Street.
desc: Four moss walls will bring life to underplanted areas of Cambridge! These walls can be customized with benches or solar charging stations, harnessing the low-maintenance, high-impact qualities of moss to clean our air and beautify our squares.

name: Upgrade the Gately Youth Center
desc: The Gately Youth Center is in need of an upgrade.  Updating the furniture and music studio as well as renovating the kitchen would bring more youth and foster stronger community at the center.

name: Smarter Cleanup for a Smart City
locationText: 9 distinct locations with high foot traffic.
desc: A cleaner, more connected Cambridge is here, by way of hands-free, solar-powered BigBelly bins. The new, foot-pedal operated trash and recycling compactors can provide free local WiFi, cut carbon emissions, and conserve City resources.

name: Enhancements to the Central Square Library
desc: Update the Central Square Library and expand the variety of items for loan. Proposed enhancements are new furniture, a laptop kiosk, and fun, non-traditional items for loan. These improvements would benefit the neighborhood and community.

name: Make Our Playgrounds Fun for All Ages & Abilities
desc: Add 4 inclusive elements to playgrounds as they are renovated, allowing people of all ages and abilities to interact with and enjoy parks and recreation areas and to encourage expanded funding of these elements in the future.

name: Public WiFi for Inman Square and Russell Field
desc: WiFi is essential to everyday life for many people.  Installing access points to offer free WiFi in the public spaces surrounding Inman Square and Russell Field would benefit many Cambridge residents.

name: Benches for a Walkable City
desc: Install 12 benches along key corridors in Cambridge so that people of all ages and abilities can enjoy benches for resting, talking, tinkering with electronic devices, people watching, and being outdoors.

name: Bicycle Safety for Cambridge Youth
desc: Access to bicycle safety equipment for youth will enable more people to enjoy this healthy activity.  It will also relieve some of the stress on public transportation, while decreasing the city’s carbon and toxic gas emissions.

name: Murals to Inspire Cambridge Youth
desc: While Cambridge is enriched by individuals studying or working in Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math (STEAM) fields, there are many young people who do not have role models who look, talk, or live like them.

name: Making Danehy Friendlier and Healthier
desc: Danehy’s signage can be confusing. Fitness stations are hard to find and people work out on benches. The City will improve fitness options for adults, add seating in the dog park, and revamp signage to show everybody what Danehy has to offer.

name: Sheltered Bike Parking at the Main Library
locationText: At the Library entrance on Broadway.
desc: The Main Library needs more bicycle parking. A glass pavilion, protecting bikes from the weather, landscaped with paths and trees, will be an attractive and functional addition to the library grounds.

name: Digital Bike Counters with Open Data
desc: What’s the impact of the new bike lanes in Cambridge? Let’s measure it! Three new bicycle counters will provide accurate counts of people passing on bicycle via in-ground loop detectors and digitally display how many people use bike lanes.

name: Urban Bicycle Wash Stations
desc: Bicycle owners need to clean and care for their bikes, ideally monthly. But for apartment dwellers, this is really hard! These centrally located bicycle wash stations would allow bicycle owners to wash off dirt, grime, and salt from their bikes.

name: Interactive Conversation Benches
desc: The benches will use recordings designed to facilitate interpersonal interaction between people who would not normally interact. The structures will include instructions and conversation prompts to encourage residents to share perspectives.

name: Trees, please!
locationText: City-wide, particularly heat islands and urban corridors.
desc: Let’s plant 100 trees around Cambridge to combat heat, provide shade cover, and reduce carbon emissions all while contributing to a healthier, happier Cambridge.

name: Water Fountains in Every Park
desc: Install new water fountain/bottle-fillers at up to 9 parks that lack drinking water fixtures. If this initiative wins, funding will be complete for water fountain installation in most of the City owned parks.

name: Protect the Health and Safety of our Firefighters
desc: This proposal will purchase and install six gear drying units to shorten wait time for clean gear ($51,000), and eleven sets of wireless headsets to protect hearing and improve communication ($55,000). Let’s protect those who protect us.

name: Smoother Cycling
desc: Improve safety, comfort, and usability of existing bicycle infrastructure by funding a series of bicycle lane repaving projects.

name: Clean Up Cambridge
locationText: Replacing existing open bins throughout Cambridge.
desc: This project will upgrade existing trash barrels and recycling containers. This will keep the streets clean, prevent pests from being drawn to waste bins, and make it easier to properly dispose of different kinds of waste.

name: Rain Gardens for Resiliency
locationText: Huron @ Cushing, Chestnut Street, Webster Avenue.
desc: Green infrastructure has never looked so good! Bioswales are engineered gardens with special soil and plants to filter and absorb stormwater. They are a cost-effective, beautiful way to keep our water clean and protect our city from floods.

name: Upgrades at the Central Square Library
desc: Update the interior of the Central Square Library. The upgrade will include new furniture that is more modern and comfortable, a new technology table that allows for easy laptop hook-up, and scanners, printers, and other technology.

name: Light it up
desc: Reduce traffic fatalities by placing more Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) at Cambridge’s busiest intersections.

name: Soak Up Solar Power
desc: Free, clean, renewable energy! Let’s add solar panels to the Russell Youth Center to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and save money on energy.

name: Fit, Fun, and Free: Outdoor Gyms for All
locationText: Danehy Park & near CRLS Tennis Courts.
desc: For those who wish to use gym equipment while breathing fresh air, these fitness facilities offer two outdoor gyms as alternatives to paid indoor gyms, and make working out accessible to people of all ages and abilities.

name: Technology for the Community Learning Center
desc: Support students and teachers in an English as a Second Language class at a Community Learning Center (CLC) satellite location by purchasing Chrome Books, a projector, and a portable screen to enhance their learning experience. This class has been funded to be held at least for the next 4 years.

name: Let's Rest: Picnic Tables & Benches for Our Parks
desc: Benches and picnic tables bring our community together. Installing new benches and picnic tables in up to 10 of our Cambridge parks will allow people of all ages and abilities to enjoy them for resting, talking, reading, people watching and being outdoors.

name: Charging into the Future
locationText: Cambridge Municipal Lots and Utility Poles.
desc: Let us help Cambridge drive and ride into the future with new publicly accessible electric car, bike, and scooter charging stations. Pole-mounted stations make on-street charging a reality, benefiting those who do not have dedicated driveways.

name: Thirst-mobile : Water truck with free, cold, water
locationText: At a community festival near you!
desc: Have you ever been desperately thirsty at a community event? This water truck provides free, cold water at community events throughout Cambridge! The water truck would reduce the number of plastic water bottles clogging our trash cans.

name: Swinging in the City
desc: Install six to eight porch swings in public squares and parks around Cambridge for residents of all ages to have fun and enjoy the experience of being a kid again!

name: Artwork Celebrating Same-Sex Marriage Rights
locationText: To be determined with community input.
desc: Create an art installation celebrating Cambridge as the first City in the United States to issue same-sex marriage licenses. The planning and design process will include local artists, LGBTQ+ groups and advocates, and the general public.

name: What's Your Speed?
desc: Remind drivers to slow down by deploying live speed displays on Cambridge’s busiest streets.

name: Give me Shelter!
desc: Provide a secure and dry option for cyclists at the Cambridge Main Library by building a year-round covered bike shelter.

name: Let Us Remember: Cambridge Memorial Peace Garden
locationText: A centrally accessible park in Cambridge.
desc: The Peace Garden will honor the lives of residents who fall victim to violence. It will offer a serene space for all to find refuge in the face of tragic loss, and will serve as a gathering place for community healing and connection.

name: Connecting Face 2 Face: Video Conferencing for all
locationText: Main Library, Rossi and Rindge Room.
desc: Our public libraries have conference rooms actively used by many Cambridge groups. We can expand their use by adding video conferencing to improve the accessibility of meetings, trainings, interviews, and other conversations.

name: Close the Canopy
locationText: Urban Heat Islands, especially East Cambridge.
desc: Plant 100 trees in the areas of Cambridge with the lowest canopy cover, making our most vulnerable neighborhoods healthier, cooler, and more beautiful places to live and visit.

name: Water Bottle Filling Stations for Major Squares
desc: Provide free, clean water in the major squares. Water foundations and bottle filling stations are a healthy option for hydration without disposable water bottles while reducing plastic waste.

name: Laundry Access in Public Schools
locationText: Cambridge Rindge and Latin School & Cambridge Street Upper School.
desc: Renovate a space in a Cambridge Public School and install washers and dryers for students who do not have easy access to laundry services at home, to use for their clothing and necessities.

name: Pedestrian-Controlled Crosswalk Lights
desc: Install 10 new pedestrian-controlled crosswalk lights in high-impact locations.

name: Extend Outdoor Wi-Fi
desc: 24-hour WiFi access added to public outdoor spaces near libraries and City-owned buildings.

name: Make the City Bloom with a Habitat Corridor
desc: Increase pollinator and bird life in Cambridge by planting native flowers and vegetation along this underused median strip, creating a beautiful habitat corridor linking Fresh Pond and Mt Auburn Cemetery—two major habitats crucial for biodiversity.

name: Keeping Cambridge Clean
locationText: Replacing existing open bins throughout Cambridge.
desc: Replace 10 trash barrels and recycling containers, making them rodent-proof and environmentally friendly. Big Belly trash cans will keep the streets clean, prevent pests from being drawn to waste bins, and make it easier to properly dispose of different kinds of waste.

name: Public Bathroom
desc: This proposal aims to build a third standalone outdoor public toilet in a high foot traffic area.

name: Upgrade the Moses Youth Center
desc: Improving the quality and equipment of the Moses Youth Center by adding new furniture, upgrading technology and modernizing sports equipment & supplies.

name: Because Benches Make Life A Little Easier
desc: Fifty additional benches would make public transportation more user-friendly and less stressful. Benches would also make these streets more hospitable for walking, shopping, and socializing for pedestrians of all ages and abilities.

name: Open Our Doors
desc: Let’s make our schools, libraries, and public buildings more accessible for all by adding automatic door openers to entries that are wheelchair accessible but lack this feature. The City will work with the Disabilities Commission to prioritize locations.

name: More BlueBike Stations Near Affordable Housing
desc: Install 3 new, Cambridge-owned, Bluebike Stations in neighborhoods that need more affordable and convenient access to bike sharing. This project will support economic inclusivity, helping everyone enjoy the many benefits of bike sharing.

name: Life & Lounge in the Park
locationText: TBD based on need and impact.
desc: Add alternative spaces for teens and adults to exercise and relax outside! This project will include an outdoor fitness station to make exercise accessible for more residents and hammock poles for residents to unwind outside.

name: Greener City Fleet
desc: Purchase 2 electric vehicles and 2 charging stations to accelerate Cambridge’s transition to cleaner transportation.

name: Better Bike Parking for Students and Families
locationText: Cambridge Rindge and Latin School and near McCrehan Pool.
desc: Install new covered bike parking at CRLS making biking easier for students and teachers; and also at  McCrehan Pool which is popular with families during the summer but lacks enough standard bike racks.

name: Traffic Calming Via Speedometer Signs
locationText: Per recommendation of the City staff.
desc: Add twenty-five speedometers (Speed Feedback Signs) where traffic calming measures are most needed based on existing traffic data and research.

name: My Court - Basketball Court Upgrades
desc: Upgrading Hoyt Basketball outdoor court – new flooring, pro basketball hoops (adjustable & single rimmed), coaching equipment & fresh paint.

name: Public Art: Commemorating Local Cambridge Activism
desc: Art honoring the 1971 action by Riverside neighborhood leaders including Black, Feminist, and LBTQ+ activists, who occupied the 888 Memorial Dr. building to demand affordable housing, slowing campus expansion & establishing a women’s center.

name: Canine Comforts
desc: This funding will be used to make improvements to the City’s dog parks, including adding a doggy cleaning station and adding molded dog bowls to water fountains.

name: Private Space for Nursing Parents
desc: Place a Mamava breastfeeding pod for parents in City Hall.

name: Urban Micro-Forests for Cambridge
desc: Pockets of unique trees, densely planted at select locations throughout the city, will beautify, educate, and help combat climate change. Approximately 50 trees will be planted with educational signage, bringing the forest into Cambridge.

name: Rain Gardens for Resilience
locationText: TBD consistent with Climate Adaptation Plan.
desc: Rain gardens are engineered to use specific soil and plants that absorb and filter stormwater, and are a cost-effective, beautiful way to naturally clean runoff and protect from flooding. Green infrastructure has never looked so good!

name: Bridging the Digital Divide
locationText: Community Learning Center, Cambridge Public Library.
desc: To help address digital equity, purchase 100 Chromebooks and 75 mobile hotspots (with a 2-year subscription) for the Community Learning Center and Public Library to better serve their adult learners and borrowers.

name: Bike Signals at Busy Intersections
desc: Navigating intersections can be confusing. Adding bike signals to busy intersections will help cyclists safely navigate intersections and make the roads more predictable and friendly for all.

name: Keep Cambridge Cleaner
desc: Install 6 touchless, pest-resistant Big Belly trash and recycling compactors in most needed areas. Solar-powered and more efficient than traditional bins, Big Bellies will be hands-free, reduce pests (like rats) and keep streets cleaner.

name: Swinging into Inclusivity
locationText: Location TBD based on need and impact. Some ideas include adding them to school parks and public playgrounds near schools.
desc: Place several inclusive swing sets in parks to allow children with mobility disabilities to play with able bodied children. This will take a stand against ableism by enabling kids of all abilities to play together.

name: Pedestrian-Controlled Crosswalk Lights
locationText: Citywide – Crosswalks selected based on safety metrics.
desc: Install five pedestrian-controlled flashing lights at high impact locations. Crosswalks without signals can be risky for pedestrians and confusing for both pedestrians and drivers.

name: Open our Doors - Automatic Door Openers on Public Buildings
desc: Many city buildings have heavy doors without automatic openers, often making access to these buildings a challenge. Touchless automatic door openers benefit those who are elderly, pregnant, using wheelchairs or walkers, pushing strollers, concerned about germs, or anyone who has their hands full.

name: We Need More Crosswalks
locationText: Major streets with long intervals between crosswalks.
desc: To enhance pedestrian safety and follow MassDOT recommendations, this project will add a minimum of five new crosswalks to major streets.

name: Safer Streets Around Parks and Schools
desc: Improve road safety near parks and schools by installing 3 raised crosswalks to promote safe and respectful use of the streets by drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

name: New Park Pavilion
desc: Add a new pavilion to a Cambridge public park to allow for outdoor, covered gatherings during all types of weather.

name: Waste Management Education Campaign
desc: Leverage local artists to develop an educational campaign about proper disposal of recyclables, trash and compost. This approach will decrease waste, reduce recycling/compost contamination and reduce rats by improving sanitation.

name: Add Color to our Youth Centers
desc: Paint the youth buildings in Cambridge with colors and patterns. Students and families from each youth center would participate in deciding the colors/design for each building and help with the painting to increase community involvement.

name: Listen Up! Public Meeting Space Hearing Technology
locationText: Public meeting space in a City building.
desc: Increase accessibility for people with hearing disabilities by installing technology that provides direct audio input to most hearing aid and cochlear implant users in a public meeting space such as a library or City Hall meeting room.

name: Who Let the Dogs Out?
desc: Add amenities like water fountains, waste bag dispensers, and more dog-friendly environments to two dog parks around the city-- offering a safe area for dogs and their owners to play and interact with other dogs.

name: Fast Response High Visibility Fire Hydrant Markers
locationText: Locations TBD by Cambridge Fire Department.
desc: Install high-visibility markers on fire hydrants around town to increase safety for all residents and reduce response time of the fire department by improving ease of locating hydrants in emergencies, at night, and in the snow.

name: Home Essentials for Newly Housed Residents
desc: Provide much needed supplies for previously unhoused Cambridge residents to set up their home in their new apartment. Upon leasing, these residents will receive a Home Furnishings Kit which will include bed, bath, and kitchen essentials.

name: Keep Cambridge Clean
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact.
desc: Install 10 touchless, pest-resistant Big Belly trash compactors in the most needed areas. Solar-powered and more efficient than traditional bins, Big Bellies will be hands-free, reduce rodent population and keep streets cleaner.

name: STEAM Upgrades for Youth Centers!
desc: Support learning, creativity, and fun for Cambridge’s Youth. This project funds upgraded STEAM equipment for Youth Centers: new computers, learning technologies, more creative art supplies, diverse books, gaming technology, recreational equipment, TV monitors and more!

name: Public Bathroom
locationText: To be determined based on need, impact, and space availability.
desc: This proposal will build a third standalone outdoor public toilet that is accessible 24 hours per day.

name: African American and Indigenous Peoples Historical Reckoning Project
locationText: Winthrop Square and other locations in Cambridge.
desc: Restore and expand the African American Heritage Trail in Cambridge, highlighting the accomplishments of Black Cantabrigians, and recognize the historical sites of Indigenous peoples in Cambridge and include traditional Eastern Woodland languages on City property.

name: Traffic Signals for Cyclists
desc: Navigating intersections can be dangerous while riding a bike. Adding bike signals to busy intersections that already have traffic signals will help cyclists safely cross intersections at a reasonable cost to the city.

name: Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
locationText: To be determined by City staff based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Funding will support new construction and any related maintenance for two new electric vehicle chargers in Cambridge. Each charging location would charge two cars at once.

name: Water Fountains
locationText: St. Peter’s Field, John Ahern Field, Longfellow Park (Pending Approval from the Historical Commission), Fort Washington Park (Pending Approval from the Historical Commission).
desc: Install four accessible drinking fountains for residents and visitors in high foot traffic neighborhoods and parks.

name: More Bluebike Stations for High-Need Areas
desc: Install 3 new Bluebike stations in Riverside and Cambridgeport, areas that are underserved by the current network.

name: Cambridge Works Out
locationText: To be determined based on need, impact, and space availability.
desc: Exercise is crucial to health and wellbeing. This project will install a permanent outdoor fitness station to make outdoor exercise more accessible to the Cambridge community.

name: Priase for Raised Intersections
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact. Prioritizing higher traffic residential areas near parks and schools.
desc: Install a raised intersection(s) in an underserved residential area with high volume traffic to calm streets and increase safety for pedestrian crossing.

name: Basketball Court Upgrade
locationText: To be determined by need and impact assessments. Recommendations include Hoyt Field, Columbia Park, Dana Park, Peabody, Riverside.
desc: Upgrade one outdoor basketball court with new flooring, pro basketball hoops (adjustable & single rimmed), and fresh paint.

name: The Cambridge Gambit
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact. Recommend sites include Tobin school next to the basketball court, Porter Square, The Port, East Cambridge, outside libraries.
desc: Install chess tables in parks, city squares and near libraries to foster fresh-air, brain training, and diverse intergenerational community interaction through chess and other board games!

name: Driver Speed Feedback for Safer Street
locationText: Locations will be selected for greatest impact where data indicates drivers are exceeding the speed limit.
desc: Purchase and install solar-powered traffic calming devices that provide real time driver feedback on the speed limit and current driving speed.

name: Outdoor Volleyball Court
locationText: To be determined based on need, impact, and space availability. (Proposal recommendations include: Danehy, Cambridge Common, Donnelly, or others.)
desc: Add an outdoor sand volleyball court to a public park.

name: Bicycle Parking that Doubles as Public Art
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Install 6 artist-designed bike racks will create functional public art while increasing available bike parking.

name: Restore the Noth Cambridge Mural Before It's Gone!
desc: This art display absorbs the positive energy that comes from neighbors gathering, kids play around it, it is used it as a backdrop for many pictures and it is very busy during basketball and tennis season. It must be refurbished for the benefit of the North Cambridge community!

name: Enhancing City Pollination Areas with Educational Displays
locationText: Bee pollinator areas and other locations as determined by City staff.
desc: This proposal funds educational displays on the importance of pollination for urban environmental sustainability to enhance current (and future) pollinator areas across the city.

name: Nursing Pod for Breastfeeding and Pumping
locationText: A City owned building. Location to be determined based on need, impact, and space availability.
desc: Provide a clean, comfortable, and safe place for those who need to breastfeed babies or pump breast milk.

name: Community Garden Storage Sheds
locationText: Community gardens around Cambridge. To be determined by need and impact assessments.
desc: Funding will support the installation of up to ten lockable sheds for tool storage at Cambridge community gardens.

name: Trees for Danehy Park and Cambridge
locationText: Danehy Park and additional areas determined by the City.
desc: Trees provide many benefits like shade, wildlife habitat, and natural beauty. Trees also help with carbon storage, stormwater control, and improved air quality. This proposal will plant new trees in Danehy Park and other needed areas around Cambridge.

name: Technology for Youth Centers
desc: This project will install built-in speakers, new computers, and tablets in youth centers. This technology will help students complete schoolwork, access new learning tools, and have fun.

name: Look and Listen: Safer Crossing for Cambridge
locationText: To be determined by City staff based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Install pedestrian crosswalk signals that vibrate with audio at 10 locations and rapid flashing beacons at 5 locations in Cambridge. This equipment will provide greater visibility and safety at crosswalks throughout the city.

name: Smart Recycling and Trash Compactors
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Add 5 touchless rodent-resistant “Big Belly” recycling and trash compactors in Cambridge. Big Belly bins are solar-powered and more efficient than traditional bins. They keep the City cleaner, reduce the rodent population, and increase access to recycling.

name: Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
locationText: To be determined by need and impact assessments. Target locations include municipal parking lots, streets with electrical infrastructure, and where demand exists.
desc: Install electric vehicle charging stations at two locations. Electric vehicles are becoming more popular, but not everyone can charge them at home. Public chargers encourage electric car use and benefit our environment.

name: E-cargo Bikes for Watering Trees
desc: E-cargo bikes help City staff maintain our urban canopy. During droughts and heat waves, E-cargo bikes transport equipment across Cambridge to water trees. Purchasing three new E-cargo bikes would expand the City’s ‘water-by-bike’ program.

name: More Outdoor Public Wi-Fi
desc: Add outdoor public Wi-Fi to Clement Morgan Park near Central Square. This proposal will further advance equitable internet access to Cambridge residents.

name: Three new Public Art Murals
locationText: The Port, Mid Cambridge, North Cambridge.
desc: Revitalize Cambridge with 3 new neighborhood murals. This public art project would reflect our cultural diversity, strength, and positive energy. Local artists working with high school students would produce the murals.

name: Basketball Renovations
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Basketball is a popular sport in Cambridge. Let’s improve our courts to make exercise more appealing and fun! This improvement project will resurface two neglected basketball courts, install new rims and nets, and repaint faded lines.

name: Bike Parking and Bike Repair Stations
locationText: To be determined based on need, impact, and space availability.
desc: Biking infrastructure doesn’t end with bike lanes. This project will construct a bike shelter with 20 covered spaces. Install 50 new bike racks with a capacity for 100 bikes and install 10 new bike repair stations.

name: Expand Access to BlueBikes
desc: Install 3 new Bluebikes stations in areas of need to expand the current network. Each Bluebikes station will increase access to riders with 19 docks and 12 bikes. Vote to support affordable and sustainable transportation!

name: Sit and Recharge in the Shade
locationText: To be determined based on need, impact, and space availability. Recommended locations include parks and city squares.
desc: Install 10 shaded benches with solar power charging stations around Cambridge. This project will improve the daily quality of life for pedestrians. These solar benches will allow people to sit out of the sun and charge their electronic devices.

name: Outdoor Gym
locationText: A public park in Cambridge. To be determined by need and feasibility assessments.
desc: Installing outdoor workout equipment in local parks encourages people to exercise. This equipment would include pull-up and dip bars, benches, and locations for stretching. Outdoor gyms help keep Cambridge residents healthy and fit!

name: Automatic Doors for Libraries
locationText: Recommended locations include O’Neill, Collins, and O’Connell Branch Libraries.
desc: This project would install automatic doors at multiple branches of the Cambridge Public Library. Automatic doors will help make libraries more accessible to the public.

name: Enhance the Moore Youth Center Exterior
desc: This project will improve the exterior of the Moore Youth Center by adding a small garden, better tables, outdoor seating, an art installation, and more. These improvements will make the area more comfortable and youth friendly.

name: Let's Play Pickleball
locationText: Tennis courts at Glacken Field and Hoyt Field.
desc: Let’s make the game of pickleball available to Cambridge community members at multiple locations! This proposal will add adjustable nets, regulation pickleball lines, signage, and benches to the tennis courts at Glacken Field and Hoyt Field.

name: Let's Play Chess
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Install outdoor chess tables in parks, city squares, and near libraries. This project will encourage community interaction through chess, checkers, and other board games! This project will ensure that residents can borrow chess sets from public libraries.

name: Finding Your Way at Danehy Park
desc: This proposal will install new signs and maps at Danehy Park. Existing signs are broken, outdated, or missing making it difficult to navigate the 50-acre park. New signs will make Danehy inviting and easy to navigate for all visitors.

name: Visual Communication Boards in Playgrounds
locationText: Public parks in Cambridge. Locations will be determined by need and impact assessments.
desc: This project will install visual communication boards in playgrounds for children who have difficulty with verbal communication. This tool allows children and caregivers to point to images to communicate their needs and desires.

name: Digital Map for Navigating Cambridge
locationText: A high-density area or near transit stations at major squares.
desc: Install a digital sign to help with public navigation. This project will provide a street map, list public transportation routes and community landmarks (libraries, parks, schools, etc.), and include information about upcoming events and important announcements.

name: Free Menstrual Care and Infant Hygiene Products
locationText: City-owned properties (Cambridge Public Libraries, fire departments, city department buildings, youth centers).
desc: People who cannot afford hygiene products are forced to make difficult decisions. Help expand accessibility of menstrual and hygiene care products to include diapers, baby wipes, and other products in City buildings for three years.

name: Additional Supplies for Unhoused Residents
desc: Deliver critical supplies to unhoused residents through established programs, including items such as socks, hats, gloves, hand warmers, feminine hygiene products, and other items to assist people living in unsheltered situations.

name: Expanding Space for Street Trees
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Help our environment by removing pavement to expand space for new and existing trees. Removing pavement provides more soil space for tree roots, helps trees live longer and healthier, improves drainage, and reduces city heat.

name: Improve Safety for Pedestrians
locationText: Public schools, hospitals, senior living facilities.
desc: Improve safety for people who use the side walk to get to schools, hospitals, and senior living facilities. This project will install raised crosswalks, interactive speed limit signs, and flashing crosswalk signs to assist with safe travel.

name: Smart Traps for Rat Reduction
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Purchase, place, and maintain 250 additional Smart Boxes (rat traps) for rodent reduction and data collection. Adding these traps would expand existing pest control measures through 2027.

name: Smart Recycling and Trash Compactors
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Add 15 rodent-resistant, no-touch recycling and trash compactors in Cambridge. "Big Belly" bins keep the City cleaner, reduce the rodent population, and increase recycling.

name: Shaded Seats on Hot Streets
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Create 3-5 shaded seating areas in busy areas most in need of shade and seating. Each area will be 300 to 500 square feet and include shade canopies and inviting places to sit: bench swings, chairs, tables, and communal seating.

name: Public Toilet for Park Upgrade
locationText: Ongoing or upcoming renovation of a community park.
desc: Improve park accessibility and hygiene with a durable, eco-friendly, public restroom. Previously PB funded Portland Loos are being designed for Flagg Street, and Cambridge Common. This PB proposal would fund an additional location.

name: Expand Access to Veterinary Care for Seniors in Low-Income Communities
locationText: Low-income housing, senior living facilities, and other areas of need.
desc: Improve access to veterinary care for residents with financial and mobility difficulties. This proposal will provide free check-ups, vaccine clinics, pet grooming, dental care, and mobile van services for three years.

name: Electric Vehicle Chargers
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Install electric vehicle (EV) charging stations at three city-owned parking lots and other locations designated by the City. More public chargers support EV adoption, which improves air quality and benefits our environment.

name: Floating Bus Stops: Improved Safety for Cyclists and Bus Riders
locationText: To be determined based on impact and need assessments.
desc: A 'floating bus stop' is when a bus stops along the street, and a bike lane separates the bus lane and sidewalk. This project will build two floating bus stops for safer travel and benefit people walking, people on bicycles, and bus users.

name: Teen Oasis at Donnelly Field
desc: Let's create a Teen Oasis in Cambridge! Equipped with shade structures, light-up swings, and scheduled events, a Teen Oasis will provide teenagers with an accessible place to hang out, enjoy the outdoors, and socialize.

name: Extend Weekend Hours at War Memorial Pools
desc: Expand swim hours on weekends at the War Memorial pools for three years. Saturday evenings would open an hour later, and Sunday mornings would open an hour earlier. This proposal will fund the operating expenses for extended swimming time.

name: Let's Help Cambridge Residents Buy Bicycles
desc: This proposal will expand bike ownership for qualifying low-income residents. This two-year program will make bicycles available for purchase at discounted rates and provide reliable cycling transportation for residents in need.

name: Tree and Community Garden Engagement Coordinator
desc: Hire a coordinator to oversee programming and organize volunteers for tree care and community garden maintenance. This new three-year position will promote knowledge and activities for residents of all ages.

name: Build Two Bus Shelters
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Install bus shelters at two bus stops. Locations will be selected to benefit the greatest number of riders. Providing accessible, safe, and comfortable shelters encourages use of public transportation and supports the City's environmental goals.

name: Add and Maintain Bike Repair Stations
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Bike repair stations need to be fixed around the City and need a program for routine maintenance. This project will create that three-year program and expand usable tools by installing five additional stations, ensuring tools are available for all.

name: Expand Access to Free Public Wi-Fi in Inman Square
locationText: Alfred Vellucci Plaza in Inman Square.
desc: Expand internet access by installing free public Wi-Fi in Mayor Alfred Vellucci Plaza in Inman Square. This proposal will further advance equitable internet access to Cambridge residents.

name: Sand Volleyball Court
desc: Install a full-sized sand volleyball court at Buckingham Field! This will provide community members with an opportunity to connect through recreation and fun, while not taking space from existing sport courts.

name: The Cambridge Women's Heritage Project
desc: Celebrate the under-recognized contributions of diverse Cambridge women. Fund research and oral history interviews to triple the number of featured women. Redesign the current project website to boost collaboration with schools and libraries.

name: Improve Parks with Shade Structures and Seating
desc: Make parks and dog parks more comfortable for visitors by building one to two shelters with seating for rainy or sunny days. This project would also fund additional benches and tables in various parks across the city.

name: Build a Pollinator Garden in a City Park
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Pollinator gardens are gardens specifically for native plant species that provide pollinator resources for local wildlife. This project will design and plant a pollinator garden within a city part to attract and nourish native pollinators!

name: Funding for High School Clubs
locationText: Cambridge Rindge and Latin School (CRLS) for up to three years.
desc: Student clubs at CRLS currently do many great things for the community: volunteering, tutoring, academic and professional development, and more. Let's provide funding to help expand their ability to engage in the community and beyond!

name: Slower Speeds for Safer Streets
locationText: Side streets running perpendicular to main roads.
desc: Install 48 speed humps on key streets in Cambridge to reduce vehicle speeds. Speed humps enhance pedestrian safety and create safer, more livable neighborhoods. This project aims to address speeding issues and improve overall road safety.

name: Mobile Center for Hard-to-Recycle Items
desc: Instead of going to the Recycling Center, let the Recycling Center come to you! At community events, the Mobile Center can help residents recycle items without have to cross the city. Help recycle items like e-waste, books, batteries, plastic bags, and more.

name: Welcome Baby Boxes for New Parents
locationText: Citywide via the Center for Families for up to three years.
desc: Let's support new parents! Baby supplies are expensive and caring for a newborn is hard. This proposal will provide baby supplies for new parents and promote information on community resources to help ease the transition into parenting.

name: Electric Vehicle Chargers
locationText: 10 charging heads at 3 locations to be determined.
desc: Install Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations at 3 locations with 10 charging heads. EV adoption is growing steadily as measured by EV charging station data collected by the City. This proposal responds to a strong demand from residents who have indicated a need for more publicly available EV chargers.

name: Basketball Court Upgrade
locationText: To be determined based on need and impact assessments.
desc: Upgrade an outdoor basketball court! This project will resurface a court most in need of repairs, paint new lines, and install adjustable hoops or inclusive play for all ages in important community locations.

name: Moses Youth Center Upgrade
desc: Let's upgrade the Moses Youth Center! This project will add comfortable new furniture for the entire youth center, improve the gym storage for moveable equipment, and provide a new music studio for young people to use.

name: Mobile Pet Care
locationText: Low-income housing, senior living facilities, and more for up to three years.
desc: Improve access to veterinary care for residents with financial or mobility challenges. This proposal will provide free check-ups, vaccine clinics, grooming, dental care, and other services to pets of residents in need.

name: Girls' Empowerment Sports Events
locationText: War Memorial, CPS building gyms, and others for up to three years.
desc: Expand the Cambridge Sports Night for Girls to include multiple events each year for youth in elementary and upper school. These fun events let young girls try different sports in a supportive community setting!

name: Shoot for the Starts: Public STEAM Programs
locationText: Cambridge Public Libraries for up to three years.
desc: Let's support astronomy and STEAM programs at Cambridge Public Libraries to help teach about the wonders of the night sky in partnership with local astronomy and STEAM organizations.

name: Install Safe Disposal Boxes for Sharp Items
locationText: Six high-need places with waste collection for up to three years.
desc: Install boxes for safe disposal of needles, lancets, or other sharp medical tools. These boxes would be located in high-need areas to provide more safe, convenient disposal options for sharps in the city.

name: Submersible Wheelchair at Gold Star Pool
desc: Purchase submersible wheelchairs for people with mobility disabilities to use for swimming at the Gold Star Pool and beach field trips. These wheelchairs will increase access to physical activity, recreation, and community participation.

name: Bring Adventure Play to Cambridge
locationText: Program locations throughout Cambridge for up to three years.
desc: Bring adventure play to Cambridge kids! Physical adventure play promotes supervised risk-taking and fun. Ongoing events and training would help community partners to facilitate a new type of play that helps foster kids' imagination.

name: Free Sunscreen in City Parks
locationText: Parks throughout the city for up to three years.
desc: Keep Cambridge healthy and extend play time by adding free sunscreen dispensers to city parks and playgrounds! This project will fund dispenser installation and ongoing maintenance for three years.

name: Live Captioning Acessibility for City Meetings
locationText: City-owned buildings, public meeting spaces for up to three years.
desc: Let's make public meetings more accessible to deaf and hard of hearing people! This proposal will fund portable screens and staffing for live transcriptions of public meetings in city-owned buildings.

name: Free Lice Combs in Public Schools
locationText: All Cambridge Public Elementary and Upper Schools
desc: Provide free, professional-quality lice combs during outbreaks to ease costs to families. These combs have dense bristles that are recommended for wash treatments and are more effective than standard combs.

name: Fun, Educational Bike Events for Adults
locationText: Public parks, empty parking lots, bike paths for up to 2 years.
desc: Expand the City's bike safety education offerings by providing learn-to-bike and beginner urban cycling workshops for adults. More educational opportunities will empower more people to feel safe and comfortable using bikes to get around the city.

name: Accessible Mats for Public Events
locationText: Outdoor City events for up to three years.
desc: Cambridge hosts many outdoor events each year. Accessible mats can lay over unpaved terrain to ensure that more people can enjoy the beautiful green space of these events. These mats support families with strollers, wheelchairs, and other mobility aids.
